data.title: Meta plans wider use of in-house AI chips as it targets lower costs
data.description:
Meta Platforms (META) plans to put a new generation of its internally designed artificial intelligence chips into data centers in the first half of next year, with the company targeting lower energy use and costs for running AI models.

The third-generation processor, MTIA 450, code-named Arke, is currently being tested, while its successor, MTIA 500, or Astrid, is expected to complete design work in about a month and enter data centers by the end of 2027, Yee Jiun Song, Meta's VP of engineering, said in an interview with Bloomberg.

“Each one takes on a little bit more risk technologically and gets us better performance,” Song said, referring to the progression of Meta's (META) custom chips. He said that includes better performance per watt and per dollar.

The Facebook parent is working with Broadcom (AVGO) on chip designs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) on production. The company has committed to more than a gigawatt of the chips over a 12-month period, Song said, adding that it expects deployment to accelerate afterward if AI demand remains strong.

Twelve Arke chips arrived from TSMC (TSM) on September 1, with performance within 2% to 3% of simulations. The processors have already run Meta (META) models as well as models from DeepSeek (DEEPSEEK) and Alibaba (BABA), Song said.

Meta (META) canceled its planned Olympus chip, which was intended for both AI training and inference, partly because of cost concerns. The company is instead focusing on inference.

“These are the workhorse chips that we’re going to use for general-purpose inference,” Song said.

The company expects future chip generations to improve speed and throughput, with Song saying Meta (META) has “a very robust roadmap” for custom silicon.

data.title: GSK upgraded at Berenberg on growth outlook
data.description:
Berenberg upgraded GSK (GSK) to Buy From Hold, saying the company is undervalued and its "heavy discount to peers is no longer justified."

The firm increased its price target to £22 from £20 (~19% upside based on Sept. 14 close on the London Stock Exchange).

Analyst Kerry Holford said that while GSK's HIV franchise will begin to experience patent expirations in 2028, its cost savings program will support R&D and better margins.

She also highlighted upcoming pipeline catalysts, such as potential US approval of bepirovirsen for hepatitis B and neladalkib for second-line non-small cell lung cancer by the end of the year.

Within the next year, pipeline readouts include phase 3 data for the antibody-drug conjugate risvutatug rezetecan (ris-rez) in second-line small-cell lung cancer; every four month Cabenuva (cabotegravir) for HIV; and proof-of-concept data for the long-acting anti-TSLP felcorekibart for asthma.

Berenberg projects 2031 group sales of ~£39B (consensus is ~£36B).

"Recently launched assets (Exdensur, Blenrep) will contribute to growth over this time-period," Holford wrote. "The opportunity for bepirovirsen, the Nuvalent lung cancer assets and GSK/Hansoh oncology ADCs is underappreciated, in our view."

data.title: Guggenheim turns bullish on defense stocks, warns on aerospace aftermarket
data.description:
Guggenheim Securities launched coverage of 22 aerospace and defense companies with a bullish view of defense contractors and aircraft manufacturers. The firm is more cautious about commercial aerospace aftermarket suppliers as passenger traffic weakens and airlines face higher fuel costs.

The analysts said defense stocks have fallen about 25% from their March 2026 peak, while forward valuation multiples have contracted roughly 55%. Guggenheim views the decline as a buying opportunity because geopolitical threats, weapons replenishment and military modernization should support spending into the next decade.

$1 trillion budget could support growth

The firm expects the fiscal 2027 base defense budget to reach approximately $1 trillion. Investment accounts could approach $600 billion, or more than 43% of total defense spending. That compares with 32% in fiscal 2013.

For investors, the central argument is that defense companies now combine lower valuations with unusually strong revenue visibility. Publicly traded contractors’ backlogs rose 25% from a year earlier during the second quarter and 42% from the second quarter of 2024, according to Guggenheim. Expansion of manufacturing capacity could also accelerate sales as contractors replenish missile inventories and deploy newer technologies.

Guggenheim initiated Buy ratings on Applied Aerospace & Defense (AADX), BWX Technologies (BWXT), Curtiss-Wright (CW), Leonardo DRS (DRS), Karman Holdings (KRMN), Kratos Defense (KTOS), L3Harris Technologies (LHX), Lyntris (LYNX), Mercury Systems (MRCY) and Northrop Grumman (NOC). The analysts’ price targets imply average upside of about 38%.

Applied Aerospace (AADX) carries the largest projected return, with a $30 target that represents 143% upside from the price cited in the report. Other notable calls include Karman (KRMN), with 79% potential upside, Lyntris (LYNX) with 60% and Kratos (KTOS) with 58%. Guggenheim rated Moog (MOG.A)(MOG.B), Redwire (RDW) and York Space Systems (YSS) as Neutral.

L3Harris offers a restructuring opportunity

L3Harris (LHX) is Guggenheim’s differentiated large-cap recommendation. The firm assigned the company a $365 price target, implying 49% upside from the report’s reference price of $246. Guggenheim believes asset sales, business separations and industry consolidation could unlock value beyond the benefits of higher defense spending.

The analysts acknowledged several risks to their defense thesis. These include the November elections, the federal deficit, higher interest rates and uncertainty surrounding supplemental spending. A continuing resolution also funds the government only through Dec. 11, leaving major budget decisions until after the elections.

Aircraft production and aftermarket prospects diverge

Guggenheim is also bullish on suppliers tied to new aircraft production. It expects Boeing (BA) production to grow at an 11% compound annual rate through 2030, including 15% growth for wide-body aircraft and 10% for narrow-body jets. The firm rates Howmet Aerospace (HWM), Hexcel (HXL), RBC Bearings (RBC) and Woodward (WWD) as Buy, with average potential upside of 31%.

The outlook is less favorable for aftermarket companies. Guggenheim forecasts global passenger traffic growth of only 1.8% in 2026, down from 5.4% last year. Higher fares, slower traffic and additional aircraft retirements could weaken parts demand within six to 12 months. The firm initiated Neutral ratings on AAR (AAR), Heico (HEI), StandardAero (SARO), TransDigm (TDG) and VSE (VSEC).

data.title: Tenet Healthcare slips after $2.6M insider sale
data.description:
• Tenet Healthcare (THC) traded lower as markets opened Tuesday after Richard Mark, one of its directors, disclosed the sale of more than $2.6M worth of shares of the hospital operator.
  • In a regulatory filing on Monday, Mark reported selling 10K shares of Tenet Healthcare (THC) for an average price of $263.42 each. The transaction, worth $2.63M, took place on Thursday, cutting his ownership in Tenet (THC) by roughly 28% to about 25.1K shares.
  • His divestment comes as the Dallas, Texas-based firm trades nearly 40% above its year-ago level.  
  • Wall Street has remained bullish on Tenet (THC) stock, with an average rating of Strong Buy from analysts, while Seeking Alpha authors indicate THC as a Buy. However, SA’s Quant System, which consistently beats the market, rates THC as a Hold.

data.title: Silver Lake, Intel-backed Altera files confidentially for IPO
data.description:
Silver Lake and Intel-backed chipmaker Altera has confidentially filed for an initial public offering.

The company has not yet disclosed the size of the offering or a price range, according to an announcement Tuesday. An earlier Reuters report indicated that the company could raise more than $2B in the offering.

Altera develops programmable chips used in areas including artificial intelligence, industrial automation, and robotics. Last April Intel (INTC) agreed to sell 51% of its stake in Altera to Silver Lake.

According to a previous report, Silver Lake has hired Barclays (BCS), Citi (C), JPMorgan (JPM), and Morgan Stanley (MS) as underwriters for the IPO.

data.title: Pre-midterm rate hike bets double as policy too stimulative – BofA survey
data.description:
Instituional investor expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike before the November U.S. midterm elections have surged, according to the latest Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey.

The September survey revealed that 41% of fund managers now expect the Fed to raise rates before the midterms, up sharply from 22% in August.

Over the same period, the proportion of investors confident that the central bank will refrain from hiking dropped to 52% from 72%.

 

The hawkish shift mirrors broader market positioning ahead of the central bank's decision on Wednesday, with data from CME FedWatch indicating a 92% market-implied probability of a rate hike, up from around 60% just a week earlier. These soaring hike expectations are primarily driven by sticky inflation remaining well above the 2% target and surprisingly robust August payroll data.

Adding to pressures on Fed tightening, fund managers noted growing unease over current financial conditions. A net 25% of surveyed investors stated that global monetary policy is currently "too stimulative," marking the highest level for this metric since September 2022.

data.title: Netskope receives Overweight rating due to durable 20%-plus growth: Stephens
data.description:
Stephens initiated coverage on Netskope (NTSK) with an Overweight rating due in part to its position in the Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, and its ability to sustain healthy top-line growth.

"We believe that Netskope has established itself as a leader in SASE with a differentiated offering and is well-positioned to deliver durable 20%+ top-line growth complemented by margin expansion," said Stephens analyst Todd Weller in an investor report. "We believe that recent solid F2Q27 results should serve to increase confidence in the fundamental story. If Netskope can deliver similarly strong performance in 2H FY27, we believe this should be a positive catalyst for the stock through both upside to estimates and multiple expansion."

Netskope made its initial public offering exactly one year ago. Stephens set a $21 price target on the stock. It has surpassed estimates in all four of its public earnings results, including its most recent, which was the second quarter of fiscal 2027. 

"Netskope has established itself as a leader in SASE and in the SSE component of SASE, as validated by leading industry analysts," Weller noted. "We believe that Netskope has a strong and differentiated technology approach that includes its ability to deeply inspect modern cloud, API, and AI traffic, strong data security capabilities, and a high-performance SASE network."

Stephens expects Netskope's full-year fiscal 2027 annual recurring revenue to reach $1.01B, revenue of $890M and an adjusted earnings per share of ($0.15). For fiscal 2028, it expects the cybersecurity company to report ARR of $1.23B, revenue of $1.08B and adjusted EPS of $0.03.

data.title: Wrangler expands brand with new footwear line from Genesco
data.description:
Wrangler is extending its brand into a footwear line through licensing partner Genesco (GCO) with its Fall 2026 collection that features western-style footwear for men, women, and children.

The Wrangler footwear line launches September 15 on the company’s website, with availability at select U.S. retailers rolling out later in the season.

“We’ve combined Wrangler’s iconic heritage and deep connection with consumers with our footwear expertise to create a collection that is unmistakably Wrangler,” said Rick Higgins, president of Genesco Brands Group.

Wrangler, a primary brand of Kontoor Brands (KTB), is riding the coattails of a fashion renaissance in Western wear thanks to the popularity of shows like Yellowstone, the proliferation of country music festivals, and brand ambassadors that include Lainey Wilson and Cody Johnson. Wrangler’s affordability (ranging from $25 to $50), improved fit, and expanded women’s line helped fuel Q2 sales and an upbeat outlook for the remainder of the year.

During Kontoor Brands’ (KTB) second quarter earnings call, CEO Scott Baxter acknowledged the strength of the brand and its growing popularity with both men and women.

“Western sits at the heart of Wrangler's DNA, and we have never been stronger. To support this momentum, we will continue to invest behind our product innovation and demand creation platforms to solidify our position as the authority in the category,” Baxter said.

data.title: BlackRock says higher yields and higher stocks can coexist
data.description:
BlackRock argues that elevated borrowing costs and firm equity markets are not mutually exclusive, even as investors brace for a likely Federal Reserve rate increase on Wednesday.

The firm’s case rests on corporate fundamentals rather than a bet that policy or energy prices will ease quickly. Long-term Treasury yields (US10Y)(US30Y) have climbed to levels last seen around the 2007 cycle, while Brent crude (CO1:COM) has held well above $100 a barrel amid renewed Middle East supply risk, including attacks that have disrupted regional energy infrastructure. Fresh U.S. inflation readings have also pushed markets to treat a quarter-point hike as the base case. Those forces would normally compress equity valuations. 

BlackRock says they have not, because expected U.S. earnings have continued to rise. Higher profit forecasts, in the institution’s view, give stocks a buffer against a steeper discount rate and costlier energy inputs. That earnings cushion is why the asset manager is keeping an overweight view in U.S. equities even as the policy and commodity backdrop tightens. 

Markets, it argues, are weighing those macro headwinds against still-resilient company results rather than treating higher yields as an automatic sell signal. The implication is that the path of profits, not the level of rates alone, will decide whether stocks can stay constructive after this week’s Fed decision.
